subject.title: Feature: Webchat / Control UI inline button support (buttons parameter, callback RPC, capabilities config)

question: Should WebChat inline interactions use shared presentation typed actions with a new authenticated chat.callback RPC, and should WebChat regain a capability/config key or rely on always-on authenticated UI behavior?
rationale: The first implementation would define a public Gateway interaction contract, callback security semantics, and a possible replacement for a retired WebChat config surface, which automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Presentation plus authenticated RPC
options.body: Use shared presentation typed actions, add a scoped authenticated chat.callback RPC, avoid webhook routing in v1, and explicitly decide whether capability config exists.

options.title: Split contract before UI
options.body: Approve the schema/RPC/auth contract first and leave Control UI rendering/click handling for a follow-up implementation issue.

options.title: Defer interactive WebChat
options.body: Keep WebChat text-only for now and route broader message reactions/feedback work through the larger WebUI interaction tracker.

recommendation.title: Presentation plus authenticated RPC
recommendation.body: Use shared presentation typed actions, add a scoped authenticated chat.callback RPC, avoid webhook routing in v1, and explicitly decide whether capability config exists.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current-history owner for the affected Gateway protocol, docs, and Control UI chat surfaces.
